title: Exercise 1: Creating and reading profile cards
lessonSummary: Great! You create dictionaries and read values by their key.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: create a dictionary and read from it.
Create a dictionary horse with the keys name ("Blitz"), breed ("Hanoverian"), age (8) and points (120). Print exactly Name: Blitz and on the next line Age: 8 (access with []).
The dictionary horse is given. Print the number of entries with len() as Number of properties: 4 and on the next line Breed: Hanoverian.

title: Exercise 2: Changing, adding and removing
lessonSummary: Nice! You change values, add entries and remove them again.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: change, add, remove.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horse = {"name": "Blitz", "breed": "Hanoverian", "age": 8, "points": 120}
horse["age"] = horse["age"] + 1
horse["wins"] = 3
removed = horse.pop("points")
print(f"Age now: {horse['age']}")
print(f"Removed: {removed}")
print(f"Properties: {len(horse)}")

tasks.instruction: The dictionary horse is given. Increase age with += 1 and add the new key wins with the value 3. Print exactly Age: 9 and on the next line Wins: 3.
The dictionary horse is given. Remove the key breed with pop() and print the removed value as Removed: Hanoverian. Then delete the key points with del and print Properties: 2 (len).

title: Exercise 3: Safe access with get() and in
lessonSummary: Well done! You ask with get() and in instead of risking a KeyError.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: get() with a default value and in.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horse = {"name": "Blitz", "breed": "Hanoverian", "age": 8, "points": 120}
print("Name:", horse.get("name"))
print("Wins:", horse.get("wins", 0))
print("Present:", "wins" in horse)

tasks.instruction: The dictionary horse is given (without wins). Fetch the value of wins with get() and default value 0 and print exactly Wins: 0.
The dictionary horse is given. Check with in and print exactly age present: True and on the next line wins present: False.

validation.expected:
age present: True
wins present: False

title: Exercise 4: Looping through dictionaries
lessonSummary: Great! You walk through a dictionary with keys(), values() and items().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: items() and values().
The dictionary feed is given (Feed store: name and amount). With items(), print each entry as Name: Amount on its own line, e.g. Oats: 3.
The dictionary feed is given. Add up all amounts with values() and print exactly Total: 10 and on the next line Kinds: 3 (len).

title: Exercise 5: Tuples
lessonSummary: Nice! You pack values into tuples and unpack them again.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: create, read and unpack a tuple.
tasks.codeTemplate:
gear = ("Saddle", 15, "Leather")
print(gear)
print("Length:", len(gear))
print("First:", gear[0])
name, value, kind = gear
print(f"Value: {value}")

tasks.instruction: Create the tuple gear = ("Saddle", 15, "Leather") and unpack it into name, value and kind. Print exactly Name: Saddle and on the next line Kind: Leather.
Two points are given as tuples. Calculate the distance as the difference of the x values plus the difference of the y values (goal minus start, all positive) and print exactly Distance: 7.

title: Exercise 6: Immutable and catching errors
lessonSummary: Masterful! You catch errors with try/except instead of letting your program crash.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: catch three kinds of errors.
The tuple gear is given. In a try block, try to set gear[1] = 99, catch the TypeError and print exactly Error: protected.
The dictionary feed is given. In a try block, try to read feed["Sugar beet"], catch the KeyError and print exactly Not in store: Sugar beet.
The input text = "ten" is given. In a try block, convert it to number with int(). Catch the ValueError and then set number = 0. Print exactly Number: 0.

title: Exercise 7: Nested structures
lessonSummary: World class! You nest dictionaries, lists and tuples.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: read nested data and filter.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horse = {"name": "Blitz", "breed": "Hanoverian", "age": 8, "points": 120, "equipment": {"saddle": "Leather", "blanket": "Wool"}}
print(f"Saddle: {horse['equipment']['saddle']}")
horses = [
    {"name": "Blitz", "breed": "Hanoverian", "age": 8, "points": 120},
    {"name": "Storm", "breed": "Haflinger", "age": 12, "points": 150},
    {"name": "Luna", "breed": "Icelandic", "age": 6, "points": 90},
]
print(f"Count: {len(horses)}")
strong = [e["name"] for e in horses if e["age"] > 7]
print(f"Strong: {strong}")

tasks.instruction: The list horses with three dictionaries is given. Print exactly Count: 3 and on the next line Last: Luna (name of the last entry, index -1).
The dictionary horse contains the sub-entry equipment and is given. Print exactly Saddle: Leather and on the next line Blanket: Wool.
The list horses is given. With a list comprehension, collect the names of all entries whose age is greater than 7 into strong and print exactly Strong: ['Blitz', 'Storm'].

title: Debug Quest
lessonSummary: All bugs found! With dictionaries and tuples, commas, keys and immutability matter.

tasks.instruction: 🐛 Bug #1 – Goal: The program should print Name: Blitz. What is wrong?
🐛 Bug #2 – Goal: The program should print Position: (150, 200). What is wrong?
🐛 Bug #3 – Goal: The program should print Age: 8. What is wrong?

Step 3 – List of profile cards: The list horses is given. Print exactly Count: 3 and on the next line Second: Storm (name of the second entry).

title: Mission 2: The Gear Shelf
lessonSummary: Mission accomplished: Tuples, unpacking and a catalog work together!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Unpack a tuple: The tuple gear is given. Unpack it into name, value and kind and print exactly Gear: Saddle, Value: 15 and Kind: Leather on three lines.
Step 2 – Catalog: The dictionary catalog (name → tuple) is given. Print exactly Value: 15 (second element of the tuple of Saddle) and on the next line Entries: 2.

Step 3 – Distance: Write a function distance(a, b) that receives two point tuples (x, y) and returns the difference of the x values plus that of the y values (b minus a, all positive). For (2, 3) and (6, 6) print exactly Distance: 7.

title: Mission 3: The Horse Roster
lessonSummary: Mission accomplished: Searching, counting and averaging across a whole list of profile cards!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Loop: The list horses with four dictionaries is given. Print each entry as Name: Age on its own line, e.g. Blitz: 8.

Step 2 – Search: The list horses is given. Write a function find_horses(items, kind) that returns the names of all entries with this breed as a list. For "Hanoverian" print exactly Found: ['Blitz', 'Wind'].
Step 3 – Statistics: The list horses is given. Calculate the average of age (sum divided by len) and print exactly Average: 8.25.

title: Extra Challenge 3: The Stable Archive
lessonSummary: The archive stands: searching, counting and a ranking from four profile cards!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create: Create the list horses with four dictionaries (keys name, breed, age): Blitz (Hanoverian, 8), Storm (Haflinger, 12), Luna (Icelandic, 6), Wind (Hanoverian, 7). Print exactly Count: 4.

Step 2 – Search: The list horses is given. Write a function find_horses(items, kind) that returns the names with this breed. Print exactly Hanoverian: 2 and on the next line Haflinger: 1 (number of hits).

Step 3 – Ranking: The list horses is given. Collect all age values, sort them in descending order and find the name with the highest value. Print exactly Best: Storm and on the next line Ranking: [12, 8, 7, 6].

title: Extra Challenge 4: The Great Stable Archive
lessonSummary: The great review is done: functions, lists and randomness from weeks 5 to 7 – now with dictionaries!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Function with return (week 5): Write create_horse(name, kind, level) that returns a dictionary with the keys name, breed, age. Call it with ("Blitz", "Hanoverian", 8) and print exactly Created: Blitz and on the next line Age: 8.

Step 2 – List of dictionaries (week 5/6): Write create_training(name, difficulty) that returns a dictionary with name, difficulty and status "open". Create the list trainings and add three Training entries with append() (Practice jumping / 1, Plan a ride / 2, Groom the coat / 3). Print exactly Training count: 3 and on the next line Status: open (status of the first one).
Step 3 – Find the largest value (week 6): The dictionary prices (name → price) is given. Find the most expensive item with a loop and print exactly Most expensive item: Oats (30).
Step 4 – Counting with a dictionary: In word = "horsestable", count how often each letter occurs. Use counter = {} and counter[c] = counter.get(c, 0) + 1. Print exactly s: 2.
Step 5 – Randomness (week 7): The dictionary feed is given. With random.choice(list(feed.keys())), draw a name into drawn and print exactly Drawn valid: True (drawn in feed).

Step 6 – Catch errors (week 5/8): The dictionary feed is given. Write amount_of(name) that returns the amount – or 0 if the name is missing (try/except KeyError). Print exactly Oats: 3 and on the next line Sugar beet: 0.
